title: Lesson 27: The 30-Day On-ramp: One Skill a Week, a Short Daily Practice
description: A schedule that turns short daily practice into a transferable AI skill: one skill a week, sessions that use the skill on real work, and a rhythm a whole organization can run together.

questions.question: Per the lesson "The 30-Day On-ramp: One Skill a Week, a Short Daily Practice", which two learning-science findings carry the design?
options: The spacing effect and the testing effect
The Pareto principle and the Dunning-Kruger effect
The Zeigarnik effect and the halo effect
The sunk-cost effect and the recency effect
questions.explanation: The lesson says both findings have been replicated for decades and that together they yield a training rhythm nearly matched to how human memory works.

questions.question: What does the lesson say the spacing effect means for training design?
options: That total practice time matters more than when the practice happens
That the same minutes split across days stick far better than the same minutes stacked into one marathon
That everyone should study at the same hour of the day
That a half-day workshop is the most efficient format
questions.explanation: The lesson cites the vocabulary demonstration in which spaced sessions retained far more than one long session of the same total time, purely because of when the sessions happened.

questions.question: What does the lesson draw from the testing effect, or retrieval practice?
options: Watching a training video is the most effective way to learn a skill
Re-reading documentation produces stronger learning than trying the skill
Actively using or recalling the skill on real work produces stronger learning than passively re-reading or re-watching, even though it feels harder in the moment
Retrieval practice only applies to rote memorization tasks
questions.explanation: The lesson says people underestimate the testing effect because easy re-reading feels more productive while it is happening, and it uses that finding to require daily sessions that use the skill on real work.
